answer_part: The CONTROL device formulation lacks methylammonium chloride (MACl), which is critical for optimizing perovskite film quality. Without MACl, the perovskite layer exhibits excessive grain boundaries and pinholes due to rapid, uncontrolled crystallization during spin-coating. This morphology increases trap-assisted recombination at grain boundaries and interfaces, directly limiting the fill factor (FF) to 78.585% and open-circuit voltage (Voc) to 1.0245 V. Additionally, incomplete surface coverage promotes shunting pathways and ion migration, further reducing FF and stability. The short-circuit current density (Jsc) of 21.189 mA/cm² is constrained by inefficient charge extraction from defective grains. While the Me-4PACz SAM (0.33 mg/mL) aids energy-level alignment, it cannot compensate for bulk perovskite defects. MACl addresses these limitations by acting as a crystallization regulator: during film formation, MACl’s volatile nature slows crystallization kinetics, enabling larger, more uniform grains with fewer boundaries. This reduces deep-level traps and suppresses non-radiative recombination, directly boosting Voc and FF. MACl also passivates undercoordinated Pb²⁺ ions and halide vacancies via chloride incorporation, mitigating ion migration and hysteresis. However, excess MACl risks residual chloride phases that could widen the bandgap or impede charge transport; the optimal concentration balances crystallization control without introducing new defects. The improved formulation increases Jsc by enhancing charge-carrier mobility and extraction efficiency, while the higher FF stems from reduced series resistance and recombination losses. Trade-offs include a slight Voc reduction due to chloride-induced bandgap narrowing, but this is offset by significant FF and Jsc gains. The optimized device achieves a PCE between 17.4% and 18.9%, with Voc between 0.959 V and 0.999 V, Jsc between 21.75 mA/cm² and 22.15 mA/cm², and FF between 83.6% and 85.6%. To implement this: dissolve MACl at 10.0 mg/mL directly into the perovskite precursor solution containing Cs₀.₀₅MA₀.₁₆FA₀.₇₉I₂.₉Br₀.₁ (1.73 mol/L), maintaining the Me-4PACz SAM concentration at 0.33 mg/mL.
control_device_fabrication: PSCs based on additives achieved a PCE of 17.059%, with a VOC of 1.0245 V, FF of 78.585%, and JSC of 21.189 mA/cm². By dissolving Cs0.05MA0.16FA0.79I2.9Br0.1 at 1.73 mol/L as the primary ingredient, the perovskite precursor was effectively prepared. Incorporating Me-4PACz (0.33 mg/mL) as a SAM was critical to adjust interfacial energy levels and refine the perovskite interface.  The perovskite solution was deposited on the substrate and spun cast at 1000 rpm for 10 s followed by 5000 rpm for 30 s. 160 µL CB was dropped on the perovskite film at 6 s before the end of the program. To lock in the desired crystal phase, the film was heated at 110 °C for 25 min.
target_device_fabrication: The PSCs achieved a champion power conversion efficiency (PCE) of 18.178%, with VOC of 0.97906 V, FF of 84.608%, and JSC of 21.945 mA/cm². Starting with a Cs0.05MA0.16FA0.79I2.9Br0.1 (1.73 mol/L) solution, the perovskite precursor was carefully crafted for optimal performance. The Me-4PACz solution was prepared with a concentration of 0.33 mg/mL. The presence of MACl (10.0 mg/mL) was crucial. The perovskite solutions were spin-coated at 1000 rpm for 10 s (acceleration rate 500 rpm/s) and 5000 rpm for 30 s (acceleration rate 1000 rpm/s), respectively. During the spin-coating process, 160 µL of CB antisolvent was quickly dripped onto the centre of the perovskite film 6 s before the end of the process. The substrates were immediately transferred to the hotplate and annealed at 110 °C for 25 min.
